label: eq:core-path-form-comparison
title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(K_L^{\rm nn}\) be the unit-conductance nearest-neighbour square
Laplacian.  The backbone in \eqref{eq:backbone-hypothesis} gives the form
inequality
\begin{equation}
 K_{G_L^J}\geq j_{\rm bb}K_L^{\rm nn}.
 \label{eq:core-path-form-comparison}
\end{equation}
The standard square Poincar\'e inequality therefore proves
\eqref{eq:core-volume-gap}.  The graph contains the nearest-neighbour
square with conductance \(j_{\rm bb}\), so Rayleigh monotonicity and the
standard dyadic-shell unit flow give \eqref{eq:core-resistance}.

Fix \(a\in B_L\).  The nearest-neighbour square with \(a\) deleted is
connected for \(L\geq3\).  To retain the resistance bound, take a
nearest-neighbour unit flow between two vertices and remove its edges
incident with \(a\).  The currents entering the at most four neighbours
of \(a\) sum to zero.  Transport the positive currents to the negative
currents along paths of length at most four in the surrounding
\(3\)-by-\(3\) square, intersected with \(B_L\) at a side or corner.
Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the energy of this local detour by a fixed multiple
of the energy on the removed incident edges.  The resulting flow avoids
\(a\) and has energy at most \(C\log(2L)\).  Rayleigh monotonicity then
proves \eqref{eq:core-punctured-resistance} for \(G_L^J\).

For the decorated graph let \(P\) be the projection onto the uniform
fibre vector and \(Q=I-P\).  Its one-particle Laplacian is
\begin{equation}
 K_{G_L^J}\otimes P+M_{d_J}\otimes Q,
 \qquad d_J(x)=\sum_{y\in B_L}J(y-x)\geq2j_{\rm bb}.
 \label{eq:decorated-backbone-split}
\end{equation}
Here \(M_d\) denotes multiplication by \(d\). This proves the decorated gap.  For resistance, fan a unit current from
one fibre vertex uniformly through the fibres over a nearest-neighbouring
base vertex, route the resulting base current through the preceding
flows, and reverse the fan at the endpoint.  The two fans have bounded
energy and the routed part has energy \(O_{J,r}(\log L)\).  After deleting
one decorated vertex, use the punctured base flow when \(r=1\).  When
\(r\geq2\), redistribute the current over the remaining \(r-1\) fibres
above that base point.  Concretely, choose one nearest-neighbouring base
vertex and replace every current through the deleted fibre by two-edge
paths through its surviving fibres.  The conductances on these paths are
at least \(j_{\rm bb}/r\).  At most \(r\) paths are used, so
Cauchy--Schwarz increases their energy by only an \(r\)-dependent factor.
This proves the punctured decorated bound.

label: lem:resistance-point-trace
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(\overline g=n^{-1}\sum_yg(y)\).  Jensen's inequality gives
\(\|\overline g\|^2\leq n^{-1}\sum_y\|g(y)\|^2\).  The variational
definition of resistance, applied after scalar projection onto an
arbitrary unit vector of \(\mathcal K\), gives
\(\|g(x)-g(y)\|^2\leq R_{\rm eff}^G(x,y)\mathcal E_G(g)\).
Average this inequality over \(y\) and use
\(\|g(x)\|^2\leq2\|\overline g\|^2+
2\|g(x)-\overline g\|^2\).

label: lem:finite-range-bose-trace
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Expand \(-\log(1-e^{-x})=\sum_{m\geq1}e^{-mx}/m\) and apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-range-heat-trace}, splitting at
\(M=\lfloor L^2/s\rfloor\geq1\). The bulk term gives
\(L^2\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{-a})/(4\pi s\sqrt{\det A_J})\), up to the uniform error
\[
 \frac{L^2}{s}\sum_{m>M}\frac{e^{-ma}}{m^2}\leq C.
\]
The large-time estimate \eqref{eq:finite-range-large-time-heat} bounds
the remaining heat-trace tail by
\(C_J\sum_{m>M}m^{-1}e^{-c_Jms/L^2}\leq C_J\).
For \(m\leq M\), the boundary, constant, and local-limit errors sum to
\[
 C_J\left[
 \frac L{\sqrt s}\sum_{m\leq M}m^{-3/2}
 +\sum_{m\leq M}m^{-1}
 +\frac{L^2}{s^2}\sum_{m\leq M}m^{-3}
 \right].
\]
These are bounded by \(C_J\mathcal R_L(s)\). All error estimates use
only \(e^{-ma}\leq1\), hence are uniform in \(a\geq0\).

label: lem:general-projected-entropy
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write \(\langle X\rangle_0=Z_0^{-1}\operatorname{Tr} Xe^{-\beta K}\).
The cutoff satisfies
\[
 0\leq I-\mathcal P^2\leq\frac12
 \sum_{x\in\Lambda}n_x(n_x-1).
\]
Wick's rule gives \(\langle n_x(n_x-1)\rangle_0=2\rho_x^2\),
which proves the normalization bound.

The nonzero spectra of \(\mathcal P e^{-\beta K}\mathcal P\) and
\(B=e^{-\beta K/2}\mathcal P^2e^{-\beta K/2}\) agree.
Since \(B\leq e^{-\beta K}\), operator monotonicity of the logarithm,
by positive regularization and passage to the limit, gives
\[
 \frac1\beta\operatorname{Tr}\Gamma_{\mathcal P}\log\Gamma_{\mathcal P}
 \leq-\frac1\beta\log Z_{\mathcal P}
 -\frac{\operatorname{Tr} K e^{-\beta K}}{Z_{\mathcal P}}
 +\frac{Z_0}{Z_{\mathcal P}}
 \langle K(I-\mathcal P^2)\rangle_0.
\]
The positive operator \(K e^{-\beta K}\) allows the cutoff inequality
to be inserted in the last trace.  To evaluate the resulting moments,
differentiate the Wick identity at fixed \(A\).  Since
\(\partial_\beta C=-AC(I+C)\), one obtains
\begin{align*}
 \langle K n_x(n_x-1)\rangle_0
 &=2\rho_x^2\langle K\rangle_0
   +4\rho_x\bigl(AC(I+C)\bigr)(x,x)\\
 &=\rho_x^2E_1
   +\rho_x\left(\frac{A}{\sinh^2(\beta A/2)}\right)(x,x).
\end{align*}
Summing over \(x\) and using \(\rho_x\leq\rho_*\) proves
\eqref{eq:general-projected-entropy}.

label: eq:regularized-bose-coefficient
title: Proof
body_md:
First suppose that \(\operatorname{supp}K\) generates \(\mathbb Z^2\). Put
\begin{equation}
 g_\eta(a):=
 \frac{\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{-a})}
      {4\pi\sqrt{\det(A_K+\eta I_2)}},
 \qquad \eta\geq0.
 \label{eq:regularized-bose-coefficient}
\end{equation}
For fixed \(\eta>0\), Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-range-quantitative} applies to
\(K_\eta\). Inserting its uniform asymptotic into
\eqref{eq:free-energy-regularization-sandwich} yields
\begin{equation}
 -c_\eta g_\eta(a)-o_\eta(1)
 \leq\beta^2S f_K(\beta,S,h)
 \leq-g_\eta(a)+o_\eta(1),
 \label{eq:scaled-free-energy-sandwich}
\end{equation}
where the errors tend to zero as \(\beta\to\infty\), uniformly in
\(h\geq0\). Since \(0\leq\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{-a})\leq\pi^2/6\),
\(g_\eta\to g_0\) uniformly on \([0,\infty)\), while \(c_\eta\to1\).
Taking first \(\beta\to\infty\) and then \(\eta\downarrow0\) proves
the required uniform limit for \(K\). For general \(J\), use
\eqref{eq:free-energy-reindexing} and
\(j_K=\widetilde j_J\) from \eqref{eq:reindexed-covariance}.
head: environment

label: rem:general-support-limitations
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:general-support-limitations}
The index \(q_J\) is essential.  For example, if the only jumps are
\(\pm2e_1\) and \(\pm e_2\), all with unit weights, the model splits into
two reindexed components. Here \(q_J=2\) and \(j_J=2\), so the two
factors cancel in the zero-field coefficient. The rank-two condition
\eqref{eq:general-kernel-hypotheses} is also essential:
a rank-one support produces decoupled one-dimensional systems and a
different temperature power.

For a general rank-two support, the proof takes first
\(\beta\to\infty\) at fixed \(\eta\) and then \(\eta\downarrow0\).
The constants in Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-range-quantitative} may diverge in the
second limit, so this argument does not give a universal explicit rate.
The rate in \eqref{eq:positive-basis-quantitative} is retained by the
present direct argument when a basis of \(\Gamma_J\) is positively
coupled.

label: lem:finite-variance-truncation
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:long-bond-path-comparison
title: Proof
body_md:
Choose \(R_0\) so that the positive bonds of \(J_{R_0}\) generate
\(\Gamma_J\).  After the reindexing of
Section~\ref{sec:general-support}, fixed words in these bonds
represent the two coordinate steps.  Concatenating translates of these words gives a path of
\(O_J(|z|)\) bonds for every \(z\in\Gamma_J\).  Project it onto the
torus and erase loops.  If \(z\notin L\mathbb Z^2\), this leaves a simple
path with distinct endpoints and no greater length.  The spin-fibre
telescoping argument in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:canonical-path-spin-comparison} therefore gives, for
every \(z\in\Gamma_J\setminus L\mathbb Z^2\),
\begin{equation}
 \sum_x\bigl(S^2-\mathbf S_x\cdot\mathbf S_{x+z}\bigr)
 \leq C_{S,J}|z|^2X_{J_{R_0},L}^{\rm per}.
 \label{eq:long-bond-path-comparison}
\end{equation}
The constant is independent of both \(z\) and \(L\), once \(L\)
exceeds a fixed bound depending only on the chosen generating words.
The first factor \(|z|\) bounds the length of the transposition word
and the second bounds the translation congestion of its path.
Multiplication by \(J(z)\) and summation over
\(|z|>R\) with \(z\notin L\mathbb Z^2\) yield
\begin{equation}
 X_{J,L}^{\rm per}-X_{J_R,L}^{\rm per}
 \leq\delta_RX_{J_{R_0},L}^{\rm per}
 \leq\delta_RX_{J_R,L}^{\rm per},
 \qquad
 \delta_R:=C_{S,J}\sum_{|z|>R}J(z)|z|^2\longrightarrow0.
 \label{eq:finite-variance-tail-comparison}
\end{equation}
This proves \eqref{eq:finite-variance-exchange-squeeze} with
\(c_R=1+\delta_R\).

Adding the same field gives
\begin{equation*}
 H_{J_R,L,h}^{\rm per}\leq H_{J,L,h}^{\rm per}\leq
 c_RH_{J_R,L,h/c_R}^{\rm per}.
\end{equation*}
Eigenvalue monotonicity and the Gibbs variational principle imply
\eqref{eq:finite-variance-free-energy-squeeze}.  Periodic and free
thermodynamic limits agree by \eqref{eq:summable-boundary-density}.

label: eq:finite-variance-covariance-limit
title: Proof
body_md:
For \(R\geq R_0\), Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-range-general} applies to \(J_R\).
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 A_{J_R}\longrightarrow A_J,\qquad
 j_{J_R}\longrightarrow j_J,\qquad q_{J_R}=q_J.
 \label{eq:finite-variance-covariance-limit}
\end{equation}
The first inequality in
\eqref{eq:finite-variance-free-energy-squeeze}, followed by
\(\beta\to\infty\), gives the required lower bound with
\(\widetilde j_{J_R}=j_{J_R}/q_J\).
For the other inequality, apply Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-range-general} at
\((c_R\beta,h/c_R)\).  Its field mass is unchanged:
\((c_R\beta)(h/c_R)=\beta h\).  The resulting coefficient differs by the
factor \(c_R^{-1}\).  First let \(\beta\to\infty\), uniformly in
\(h\geq0\), and then let \(R\to\infty\).  Equations
\eqref{eq:finite-variance-tail-comparison} and
\eqref{eq:finite-variance-covariance-limit} make both bounds coincide and
prove \eqref{eq:finite-variance-infinite-range-limit}.

label: lem:lr-local-limits
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For \(0<\sigma<2\), rescale the tail sum by \(z=|p|^{-1}x\).
The leading Riemann sum is
\[
 a|p|^\sigma\int_{\mathbb R^2}
 \frac{1-\cos(\widehat p\cdot x)}{|x|^{2+\sigma}}\,dx
 =\kappa_\sigma|p|^\sigma,
\]
where \(\widehat p=p/|p|\). Rotation invariance and
\eqref{eq:stable-symbol-constant} were used.
The error in \eqref{eq:power-law-hypothesis} contributes \(o(|p|^\sigma)\):
split at \(|z|=|p|^{-1}\) and use
\(1-\cos(p\cdot z)\leq C\min\{1,|p|^2|z|^2\}\).
For \(\sigma=2\), set
\(\omega(\vartheta):=(\cos\vartheta,\sin\vartheta)\).  The annulus
\(1\ll |z|\ll|p|^{-1}\) gives
\[
 \frac a2\int_1^{|p|^{-1}}\frac{dr}{r}
 \int_0^{2\pi}(p\cdot\omega(\vartheta))^2\,d\vartheta
 =\frac{\pi a}{2}|p|^2\log\frac1{|p|}.
\]
The remainder in \eqref{eq:power-law-hypothesis} has a finite second
moment and hence contributes \(O(|p|^2)\).

The nearest-neighbour backbone makes zero the unique zero of the symbol.
Fourier inversion, a rescaling near zero, and dominated convergence now
give \eqref{eq:lr-stable-return} and \eqref{eq:lr-marginal-return}.  In
the marginal case use
\(p=(2/(c_4u\log u))^{1/2}q\).  The same splitting of the Fourier integral,
without taking a limit, proves \eqref{eq:lr-full-heat-bound}.

label: lem:lr-finite-box-heat
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:lr-fractional-nash
title: Proof
body_md:
We first prove the finite-volume estimates used below.  Put
\(P_L=L^{-2}|\1\rangle\langle\1|\) and \(Q_L=I-P_L\).  We claim that
\begin{align}
 \|Q_Lv\|_2^{2+\sigma}
 &\leq C\langle v,K_{J,L}^Nv\rangle
       \|Q_Lv\|_1^\sigma,
 &&0<\sigma<2,
 \label{eq:lr-fractional-nash}\\
 \|Q_Lv\|_2^4
 &\leq C\langle v,K_{J,L}^Nv\rangle
       \|Q_Lv\|_1^2,
 &&\sigma=2.
 \label{eq:lr-nn-nash}
\end{align}
All norms in this paragraph are counting-measure norms.

Let \(\mathbb T_{2L}=\mathbb Z/(2L\mathbb Z)\) and
\(\mathbb T_{2L}^2=\mathbb T_{2L}\times\mathbb T_{2L}\), and let
\(\pi:\mathbb T_{2L}\to\{1,\ldots,L\}\) be the folding map
\begin{equation}
 \pi(j)=j\quad(1\leq j\leq L),\qquad
 \pi(j)=2L+1-j\quad(L<j\leq2L).
 \label{eq:lr-folding-map}
\end{equation}
Extend \(w=Q_Lv\) evenly by
\((Ew)(x_1,x_2)=w(\pi(x_1),\pi(x_2))\).  Then \(Ew\) has mean zero and
\begin{equation}
 \|Ew\|_p^p=4\|w\|_p^p,
 \qquad 1\leq p<\infty.
 \label{eq:lr-reflection-norms}
\end{equation}
For \(0<\sigma<2\), equip the torus with the form
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E_{\sigma,2L}(F)
 :=\frac12\sum_{x,y\in\mathbb T_{2L}^2}
 (1+d_{2L}(x,y))^{-2-\sigma}|F(x)-F(y)|^2,
 \label{eq:lr-torus-fractional-form}
\end{equation}
where \(d_{2L}\) is the Euclidean periodic distance.  The folding map is
one-Lipschitz from the cycle of length \(2L\) to the interval, and every
ordered pair in \(B_L^2\) has at most sixteen ordered preimages.  The
two-sided tail bound implied by \eqref{eq:power-law-hypothesis}
therefore gives
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E_{\sigma,2L}(Ew)
 \leq C\langle w,K_{J,L}^Nw\rangle.
 \label{eq:lr-reflection-form}
\end{equation}
Pairs whose projected distance is at least the fixed tail radius are
compared directly.  The finitely many remaining displacements are routed
along fixed nearest-neighbour paths. Telescoping and translation of these
paths bound their total form by the positive nearest-neighbour part of
\(K_{J,L}^N\).

For completeness, represent torus frequencies by
\(k\in\{-L,\ldots,L-1\}^2\) and put \(p_k=\pi k/L\).
Use the orthonormal Fourier convention
\(\widehat F(k)=(2L)^{-1}\sum_{x\in\mathbb T_{2L}^2}
F(x)e^{-i\pi k\cdot x/L}\).
Dyadic summation in the jump variable gives, for every nonzero torus
frequency \(p_k\),
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{z\in\mathbb T_{2L}^2}
 (1+d_{2L}(0,z))^{-2-\sigma}
 (1-\cos(p_k\cdot z))\geq c|p_k|^\sigma.
 \label{eq:lr-torus-symbol-lower}
\end{equation}
Splitting Parseval's sum into \(|p_k|\leq R\) and \(|p_k|>R\) yields
\begin{equation}
 \|F\|_2^2
 \leq CR^2\|F\|_1^2+CR^{-\sigma}\mathcal E_{\sigma,2L}(F).
 \label{eq:lr-torus-frequency-split}
\end{equation}
Optimization in \(R\) proves
\begin{equation}
 \|F\|_2^{2+\sigma}
 \leq C\mathcal E_{\sigma,2L}(F)\|F\|_1^\sigma
 \quad\text{when }\sum_xF(x)=0.
 \label{eq:lr-torus-nash}
\end{equation}
If the formal optimizer lies below \(\pi/L\), use
\eqref{eq:lr-torus-symbol-lower} at the smallest nonzero frequency.
This gives the same inequality.  If it exceeds a fixed constant, the
unit-scale part of \eqref{eq:lr-torus-symbol-lower}, together with
\(\|F\|_2\leq\|F\|_1\), gives the result directly.  Equations
\eqref{eq:lr-reflection-norms}--
\eqref{eq:lr-torus-nash} prove \eqref{eq:lr-fractional-nash}.  At
\(\sigma=2\), reflect only the nearest-neighbour form and repeat the same
Fourier splitting with its quadratic symbol. This proves
\eqref{eq:lr-nn-nash}.

We next derive the centered heat-kernel and trace bounds.  Let
\(T_u=e^{-uK_{J,L}^N}Q_L\), let \(F(u)=\|T_uf\|_2^2\), and set
\(\theta=\sigma\) for \(0<\sigma<2\) and \(\theta=2\) for
\(\sigma=2\).  Since the censored semigroup is Markovian,
\(\|T_uf\|_1\leq\|Q_Lf\|_1\leq2\|f\|_1\).  The two Nash inequalities
therefore imply
\begin{equation}
 F'(u)=-2\langle T_uf,K_{J,L}^NT_uf\rangle
 \leq-cF(u)^{1+\theta/2}\|f\|_1^{-\theta}.
 \label{eq:lr-nash-differential-inequality}
\end{equation}
Integration and self-adjointness give
\begin{equation}
 \|T_u\|_{1\to2}\leq Cu^{-1/\theta},
 \qquad
 \|T_u\|_{1\to\infty}
 \leq\|T_{u/2}\|_{1\to2}^2\leq Cu^{-2/\theta}.
 \label{eq:lr-centered-ultracontractivity}
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{align}
 \sup_{x,y}(e^{-uK_{J,L}^N})(x,y)
 &\leq C(u^{-2/\sigma}+L^{-2}),&&0<\sigma<2,\notag\\
 \sup_{x,y}(e^{-uK_{J,L}^N})(x,y)
 &\leq C(u^{-1}+L^{-2}),&&\sigma=2,
 \label{eq:lr-censored-kernel-bound}
\end{align}
and, because the diagonal of \(T_u\) is nonnegative,
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Tr}_{\1^\perp}e^{-uK_{J,L}^N}
 =\sum_{x\in B_L}\langle\delta_x,T_u\delta_x\rangle
 \leq L^2\|T_u\|_{1\to\infty}.
 \label{eq:lr-centered-trace-bound}
\end{equation}
This proves \eqref{eq:lr-stable-neumann-tail} and
\eqref{eq:lr-marginal-neumann-tail} for every \(u\geq1\), uniformly in
\(L\).  For \(0<\sigma<2\), these are the finite-volume analogues of
the stable-like estimates in \cite{BarlowBassKumagai2009}. The marginal
bound follows instead from \eqref{eq:lr-nn-nash}.

Let \(X_u\) be the full-lattice walk and couple it to the censored walk by
using the same jump clocks, suppressing a jump only if it leaves \(B_L\).
Let \(\tau_L\) be the first clock ring at which the proposed jump leaves
\(B_L\).  Until time \(\tau_L\) the two paths agree.  If
\(d_L(x)=\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\mathbb Z^2\setminus B_L)\), truncation of
jumps at \(d_L(x)/4\), followed by Doob's inequality for the truncated
martingale, gives
\begin{align}
 \mathbb P_x(\tau_L\leq u)
 &\leq C\min\{1,ud_L(x)^{-\sigma}\},&&0<\sigma<2,
 \label{eq:lr-stable-exit}\\
 \mathbb P_x(\tau_L\leq u)
 &\leq C\min\left\{1,
 \frac{u\log(2+d_L(x))}{d_L(x)^2}\right\},&&\sigma=2.
 \label{eq:lr-marginal-exit}
\end{align}
Here the rate of jumps longer than \(d\) is \(O(d^{-\sigma})\), while the
second moment truncated at \(d\) is \(O(d^{2-\sigma})\), or \(O(\log d)\)
at \(\sigma=2\).

Write \(p_{L,u}^N,p_{L,u}^D\), and \(p_u^\infty\) for the censored,
killed, and full-lattice kernels.  Regard every rejected clock ring of the
censored walk as a mark.  The marked path measures of the full and
censored walks agree until \(\tau_L\), and therefore
\begin{align}
 |p_{L,u}^N(x,x)-p_u^\infty(x,x)|
 \leq{}&\mathbb P_x(Y_u=x,\tau_L\leq u)
       +\mathbb P_x(X_u=x,\tau_L\leq u),
 \label{eq:lr-common-clock-difference}\\
 p_u^\infty(x,x)-p_{L,u}^D(x,x)
 ={}&\mathbb P_x(X_u=x,\tau_L\leq u),
 \label{eq:lr-killed-loop-identity}
\end{align}
where \(Y\) denotes the censored path.  For either probability in
\eqref{eq:lr-common-clock-difference}, the contribution from
\(\tau_L\leq u/2\) is, by the strong Markov property, at most
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P_x(\tau_L\leq u/2)
 \sup_{v\geq u/2,z}p_v(z,x),
 \label{eq:lr-early-exit-loop-bound}
\end{equation}
with the kernel of the corresponding walk.  Reversal of diagonal loops
moves a rejected mark or exit in \([u/2,u]\) to \([0,u/2]\) and gives the
same bound for the late contribution.  This is ordinary reversibility for
\(X\), and reversibility of the marked rejected-clock measure for \(Y\).
For \(u\leq cL^\sigma\), the \(L^{-2}\) term in
\eqref{eq:lr-censored-kernel-bound} is bounded by \(Cu^{-2/\sigma}\).
Consequently, in the stable case,
\begin{equation}
 |p_{L,u}^N(x,x)-I_J(u)|
 +|p_{L,u}^D(x,x)-I_J(u)|
 \leq Cu^{-2/\sigma}\mathbb P_x(\tau_L\leq u/2).
 \label{eq:lr-common-clock-diagonal}
\end{equation}
At \(\sigma=2\), equations \eqref{eq:lr-full-heat-bound} and
\eqref{eq:lr-censored-kernel-bound} instead give
\begin{equation}
 |p_{L,u}^N(x,x)-I_J(u)|
 +|p_{L,u}^D(x,x)-I_J(u)|
 \leq \frac Cu\mathbb P_x(\tau_L\leq u/2),
 \qquad u\leq cL^2.
 \label{eq:lr-marginal-common-clock-diagonal}
\end{equation}
Summing
\eqref{eq:lr-stable-exit} over the \(O(L)\) sites in every boundary layer
gives
\[
 \sum_{x\in B_L}\mathbb P_x(\tau_L\leq u)
 \leq CL
 \begin{cases}
  u^{1/\sigma},&\sigma>1,\\
  u\log(2+L/u),&\sigma=1,\\
  uL^{1-\sigma}+u^{1/\sigma},&\sigma<1.
 \end{cases}
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:lr-stable-finite-box-heat}. Subtracting the constant
Neumann mode accounts for the harmless \(1\).

At the marginal exponent use the second estimate in
\eqref{eq:lr-censored-kernel-bound}, rather than a sharp marginal bound.
The boundary-layer sum in \eqref{eq:lr-marginal-exit} is
\(O(LR_2(u))\).  Multiplication by \(C/u\) proves
\eqref{eq:lr-marginal-finite-box-heat}.  This deliberately conservative
estimate is sufficient for the box scale
\eqref{eq:lr-marginal-pressure-scales}, which contains an extra
logarithmic volume factor.
head: environment

label: lem:lr-bose-traces
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Expand \(-\log(1-q)=\sum_{m\geq1}q^m/m\).  In the stable case,
Lemma~\ref{lem:lr-finite-box-heat} and
\eqref{eq:lr-stable-return} give, for each fixed \(m\geq1\),
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{Tr}_{\1^\perp}e^{-msK_{J,L}^N}}
 {L^2D_\sigma t^{-\nu}}\longrightarrow m^{-\nu},
 \qquad
 \frac{\operatorname{Tr} e^{-mt h_{J,\ell}^D}}
 {\ell^2D_\sigma t^{-\nu}}\longrightarrow m^{-\nu}.
\]
Indeed, the relative boundary errors for a box of side \(n\) are bounded,
up to constants depending on \(m\), by
\[
 \begin{cases}
 t^{1/\sigma}/n,&1<\sigma<2,\\
 (t/n)\log(2+n/t),&\sigma=1,\\
 t/n^\sigma+t^{1/\sigma}/n,&0<\sigma<1,
 \end{cases}
 \quad+\frac{t^\nu}{n^2},
\]
and vanish for both prescribed box scales.  For any fixed cutoff \(M\),
convergence of the finite Bose sums is uniform in \(b\geq0\).
The Neumann tail is, by \eqref{eq:lr-stable-neumann-tail}, at most
\(CL^2t^{-\nu}M^{-\nu}\).  For the Dirichlet lower bound, discard the
positive tail.  The target polylogarithm has tail at most
\(CM^{-\nu}\), uniformly in \(b\).  Letting first \(t\to\infty\) and
then \(M\to\infty\) proves
\eqref{eq:lr-stable-neumann-bose} and
\eqref{eq:lr-stable-dirichlet-bose}.

The same fixed-cutoff argument proves the marginal Dirichlet bound.
For each fixed \(m\), \eqref{eq:lr-marginal-return} and
\eqref{eq:lr-marginal-finite-box-heat} give
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{Tr} e^{-mt h_{J,\ell}^D}}
 {\ell^2D_2/(t\log t)}\longrightarrow m^{-1}.
\]
The relative boundary error is
\(O(\sqrt t(\log t)^{3/2}/\ell+t\log t/\ell^2)=o(1)\).
Discarding the positive Bose tail and bounding the omitted dilogarithm
by \(C/M\) proves \eqref{eq:lr-marginal-dirichlet-bose}.

For the marginal Neumann trace a growing cutoff is needed because
\eqref{eq:lr-marginal-neumann-tail} is weaker.  Take
\(M=g(t)^{1/2}\).  Relative to \(L^2/(t\log t)\asymp g(t)\),
\eqref{eq:lr-marginal-finite-box-heat} gives summed boundary error
\(O(\log t/\sqrt{g(t)})\), while
\eqref{eq:lr-marginal-neumann-tail} bounds the remaining Bose series by
\(O(\log t/M)\).  Both vanish.  Equation
\eqref{eq:lr-marginal-return} and
\(\log(ms)/\log t=1+o(1)\), uniformly for \(m\leq M\), now give
\eqref{eq:lr-marginal-neumann-bose}.  All error estimates are uniform in
\(b\geq0\), since \(e^{-mb}\leq1\).

label: lem:lr-box-geometry
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:lr-two-sided-tail
title: Proof
body_md:
The hypothesis \eqref{eq:power-law-hypothesis} implies, for all sufficiently
large \(|z|\),
\begin{equation}
 c(1+|z|)^{-2-\sigma}\leq J(z)
 \leq C(1+|z|)^{-2-\sigma}.
 \label{eq:lr-two-sided-tail}
\end{equation}
The missing finitely many short displacements are supplied, when needed,
by paths in the positive nearest-neighbour backbone.  Fix a radius
\(R_0\) beyond which the lower bound in \eqref{eq:lr-two-sided-tail}
holds.  If \(v\) has mean zero, then
\[
 \frac12\sum_{\substack{x,y\in B_L\\|x-y|\geq R_0}}
 |v(x)-v(y)|^2
 \geq (L^2-C_{R_0})\|v\|_2^2.
\]
Consequently, for all sufficiently large \(L\),
\begin{align}
 \langle v,K_{J,L}^Nv\rangle
 &\geq cL^{-2-\sigma}\frac12
 \sum_{\substack{x,y\in B_L\\|x-y|\geq R_0}}
 |v(x)-v(y)|^2
 \geq cL^{-\sigma}\|v\|_2^2.
 \label{eq:lr-complete-gap-comparison}
\end{align}
The finitely many smaller boxes are absorbed by decreasing the constant,
using the nearest-neighbour Poincar\'e inequality.
At \(\sigma=2\) we retain the weaker consequence \(cL^{-2}\), which is
sufficient for Proposition~\ref{prop:lr-pressure}.

We next construct the resistance flow and keep track of its divergence.
A flow \(\theta\) is antisymmetric on ordered edges with positive
conductance, and its divergence is
\(\operatorname{div}\theta(u)=\sum_{v:J(v-u)>0}\theta(u,v)\).
Given \(x\in B_L\), choose nested sets
\begin{equation}
 \{x\}=Q_0^x\subset Q_1^x\subset\cdots\subset Q_N^x=B_L,
 \qquad r_j:=2^{j-1}r_0\wedge L\quad(j\geq1),
 \label{eq:lr-nested-flow-sets}
\end{equation}
obtained by intersecting and, near the boundary, translating coordinate
squares, so that \(|Q_j^x|\asymp r_j^2\) for \(j\geq1\).  Let
\(\mu_j^x\) be the uniform probability measure on \(Q_j^x\).  After
increasing the fixed \(r_0\), couple consecutive measures, for
\(1\leq j\leq N-1\), by
\begin{equation}
 \pi_j^x(u,v):=\mu_j^x(u)\mu_{j+1}^x(v),\qquad
 |u-v|\leq Cr_j,\qquad
 \max_{u,v}\pi_j^x(u,v)\leq Cr_j^{-4}.
 \label{eq:lr-scale-coupling}
\end{equation}
Discard the diagonal transports \(u=v\), which have zero divergence.
Orient every remaining mass \(\pi_j^x(u,v)\) from \(u\) to \(v\), and
call the resulting flow \(\theta_j^x\).  If \(|u-v|<R_0\), replace this
transport by a fixed nearest-neighbour path.  This preserves the exact
identity
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{div}\theta_j^x=\mu_j^x-\mu_{j+1}^x.
 \label{eq:lr-scale-divergence}
\end{equation}
Let \(\theta_0^x\) transport \(\delta_x\) to \(\mu_1^x\) along fixed
nearest-neighbour paths.  Because \(r_0\) is fixed, this initial flow has
bounded energy.
For every later scale, \eqref{eq:lr-two-sided-tail} and
\eqref{eq:lr-scale-coupling} give
\begin{align}
 \mathcal E_{\rm flow}(\theta_j^x)
 &:=\frac12\sum_{\substack{u,v\in B_L\\J(v-u)>0}}
 \frac{|\theta_j^x(u,v)|^2}{J(v-u)}\notag\\
 &\leq Cr_j^4(r_j^{-4})^2r_j^{2+\sigma}
       +Cr_j^2(r_j^{-4})^2
 \leq Cr_j^{\sigma-2}.
 \label{eq:lr-flow-scale-energy}
\end{align}
The second term bounds the finitely long nearest-neighbour routings.  For
a fixed graph edge, the currents contributed by all later dyadic scales
decrease geometrically.  Hence, pointwise on edges,
\begin{equation}
 \left(\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}|\theta_j^x(e)|\right)^2
 \leq C\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}|\theta_j^x(e)|^2.
 \label{eq:lr-flow-overlap}
\end{equation}
It follows that
\(\theta^x:=\theta_0^x+\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}\theta_j^x\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{div}\theta^x=\delta_x-|B_L|^{-1}\1,
 \qquad
 \mathcal E_{\rm flow}(\theta^x)
 \leq C+C\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}r_j^{\sigma-2}.
 \label{eq:lr-flow-telescoping}
\end{equation}
Thus \(\theta^x-\theta^y\) is a unit flow from \(x\) to \(y\).
Thomson's principle gives a uniform resistance diameter for
\(\sigma<2\) and an \(O(\log(2L))\) diameter for \(\sigma=2\).

The same construction gives the punctured estimate without a mass
defect.  Fix \(o\in B_L\) and \(x\in B_L\setminus\{o\}\), and replace
every set by
\(Q_j^x\setminus\{o\}\), and normalize counting measure on the resulting
set.  The product couplings retain \eqref{eq:lr-scale-coupling}.  Whenever
a fixed short path meets \(o\), detour it inside a \(3\)-by-\(3\) or
\(4\)-by-\(4\) neighbourhood. The number and length of these detours are
uniformly bounded.  The divergences telescope to
\begin{equation}
 \delta_x-|B_L\setminus\{o\}|^{-1}\1_{B_L\setminus\{o\}},
 \label{eq:lr-punctured-flow-divergence}
\end{equation}
so subtracting the flows from \(x\) and \(y\) proves the asserted
punctured resistance bound.

It remains to pass to the spin-fibre decoration.  Let \(P\) project onto
the uniform fibre vector and \(Q=I-P\).  Direct summation over the fibre
labels gives
\begin{equation}
 K_{J,L}^{(r)}=K_{J,L}^N\otimes P+M_{d_{J,L}}\otimes Q,
 \qquad d_{J,L}(x)=\sum_{y\in B_L}J(y-x)\geq c_J.
 \label{eq:lr-decorated-split}
\end{equation}
Thus the acoustic gap is the base gap and the optical gap is uniform.
Lift a base flow by distributing the current on an edge \((x,y)\)
equally among its \(r^2\) fibre edges.  Since each has conductance
\(J(y-x)/r\), the lifted energy is \(r^{-1}\) times the base energy.  A
current from a single fibre vertex is first fanned to the uniform fibre
measure by two-edge paths through a fixed inward nearest-neighbouring base
point. This costs only a constant depending on \(r\) and the backbone
weights.  Reverse the fan at the endpoint.  After deletion of one
decorated vertex, use the punctured base flow if \(r=1\). If \(r\geq2\),
distribute the current over the surviving labels above that base point and
use the same local fan.  This proves both decorated resistance estimates
in \eqref{eq:lr-box-resistance}.

body_md:
In Proposition~\ref{prop:abstract-graph-collision}, substitute
\(n=rL^2\), the degree bound, and
\eqref{eq:lr-box-gap}--\eqref{eq:lr-box-resistance}.  For
\(0<\sigma<2\), the factor
\((n\lambda)^{-1}+\rho\) is bounded and the bracket is
\(O(1+k+k^2L^{\sigma-2})\).  At \(\sigma=2\), the prefactor is
\(O(k^2\log(2L))\) and the squared bracket is

head: environment

label: lem:lr-highest-weight
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(M_m=rm^2\) and write
\[
 \mathcal E_{uv}(F)=\frac12\mathbb E_{\nu_{m,k}}
 |F(\eta^{uv})-F(\eta)|^2,
\]
where \(\nu_{m,k}\) is uniform on the \(k\)-subsets of
\(B_m\times[r]\).  The complete-graph exclusion form is
\(\sum_{\{u,v\}}\mathcal E_{uv}\), and the form of
\(H_{m,k}^{(r,J)}\) is \(\sum_{\{u,v\}}c_{uv}\mathcal E_{uv}\), with
\(c_{(x,\alpha),(y,\gamma)}=J(y-x)/r\) for \(x\ne y\) and zero
within a fibre.

Call a pair good if its base points are at distance at least the fixed
tail radius \(R_0\), and bad otherwise.  On good pairs,
\(c_{uv}\geq cm^{-2-\sigma}\).  For a bad pair, let \(W_{uv}\) consist
of decorated vertices whose base points are at distance at least
\(R_0\) from both endpoints.  For large \(m\),
\(|W_{uv}|\geq cM_m\), and the transposition identity
\((uv)=(uw)(vw)(uw)\), telescoping, and invariance of \(\nu_{m,k}\)
give
\[
 \mathcal E_{uv}(F)\leq\frac C{|W_{uv}|}\sum_{w\in W_{uv}}
 \bigl(\mathcal E_{uw}(F)+\mathcal E_{vw}(F)\bigr).
\]
Each vertex has only \(C_{r,R_0}\) bad partners, so summing yields
\[
 \sum_{\{u,v\}\,\mathrm{bad}}\mathcal E_{uv}(F)
 \leq\frac C{M_m}
 \sum_{\{u,v\}\,\mathrm{good}}\mathcal E_{uv}(F).
\]
Together with the good-pair conductance bound, this proves
\begin{equation}
 K_{M_m,k}\leq Cm^{2+\sigma}H_{m,k}^{(r,J)},
 \label{eq:lr-complete-graph-comparison}
\end{equation}
where \(K_{M_m,k}\) is the unit-conductance complete-graph exclusion
generator.  The positive nearest-neighbour backbone handles the finitely
many smaller boxes after increasing \(C\).
On the highest-weight space of total spin \(M_m/2-k\), the Casimir
identity gives
\begin{equation}
 K_{M_m,k}^{\mathrm{HW}}=k(M_m-k+1)I\geq\frac12kM_mI.
 \label{eq:lr-complete-hw-casimir}
\end{equation}
This proves \eqref{eq:lr-highest-weight}.  Bounding the multiplicity by
\(\binom{M_m}{k}\) and the number of descendants by \(M_m+1\), we obtain
\[
 \operatorname{Tr} e^{-u\mathcal H_m^{(r,J)}-b\mathcal N}
 \leq(M_m+1)\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor M_m/2\rfloor}
 \binom{M_m}{k}e^{-cuk/m^\sigma-bk}
 \leq(M_m+1)\bigl(1+e^{-cu/m^\sigma-b}\bigr)^{M_m},
\]
which implies \eqref{eq:lr-rough-trace}.

label: prop:lr-pressure
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We use the harmonic-extension relations
\eqref{eq:extension-norm}--\eqref{eq:extension-energy}, the spin
decomposition \eqref{eq:exact-field-multiplet-decomposition}, and the
cutoff argument of Section~\ref{sec:finite-range-proof}.
Their energy and particle cutoffs close with the following choices.

Suppose first that \(0<\sigma<2\), put \(\nu=2/\sigma\), and choose
\begin{equation}
 g=(\log t)^8,\qquad L^2\asymp t^\nu g,
 \qquad m^\sigma\asymp\frac{t}{A\log t},
 \label{eq:lr-stable-pressure-scales}
\end{equation}
Choose integers \(m,n\) with these asymptotics and set \(L=mn\). Then
\(m\mid L\), and all relative rounding errors tend to zero.  Delete all
positive bonds between the cells.  Lemma~\ref{lem:lr-highest-weight},
with \(A\) large and fixed, gives
\begin{equation}
 \log\operatorname{Tr} e^{-(t/2)\mathcal H_L^{(r,J)}-b\mathcal N}
 \leq Cg(\log t)^{1+\nu}=: \mathcal R_\sigma(t).
 \label{eq:lr-stable-rough-main}
\end{equation}
Indeed, there are \(O(g(\log t)^\nu)\) cells and the descendant factor in
each cell has logarithm \(O(\log t)\).  Set
\begin{equation}
 e_0:=C\frac{g(\log t)^{1+\nu}}t,
 \qquad
 K:=\lfloor c^{-1}L^\sigma e_0\rfloor
 \leq Cg^{1+\sigma/2}(\log t)^{1+\nu}.
 \label{eq:lr-stable-cutoffs}
\end{equation}
Increasing the constant in \(e_0\), the spectral inequality
\eqref{eq:high-energy-spectral-inequality} and
\eqref{eq:lr-stable-rough-main} make the contribution above \(e_0\)
exponentially small.  Equation \eqref{eq:lr-highest-weight} on the full
box excludes \(k>K\) below that energy.

For \(k\leq K\),
\begin{equation}
 K^2L^{\sigma-2}=o(1),
 \qquad
 \delta_t\leq CK^4e_0
 \leq \frac Ct g^{5+2\sigma}(\log t)^{5(1+\nu)}=o(1),
 \label{eq:lr-stable-collision-delta}
\end{equation}
where the first assertion follows from \(g=t^{o(1)}\), and the second
from \eqref{eq:lr-stable-collision}.  Harmonic extension and min--max
therefore compare the retained interacting exchange eigenvalues with the
free product eigenvalues at time
\(s=t/(1+\delta_t)\).  As in
\eqref{eq:fixed-k-field-comparison}, the field factor \(e^{-bk}\) is not
rescaled.

For \(\sigma=2\), take instead
\begin{equation}
 g=(\log t)^8,\qquad L^2\asymp t\log t\,g,
 \qquad m^2\asymp\frac{t}{A\log t}.
 \label{eq:lr-marginal-pressure-scales}
\end{equation}
Again choose the integers so that \(m\mid L\). The relative rounding
errors tend to zero.
The corresponding estimates are
\begin{align}
 \mathcal R_2(t)&\leq Cg(\log t)^3,
 &e_0&=C\frac{g(\log t)^3}{t},
 &K&\leq Cg^2(\log t)^4,
 \label{eq:lr-marginal-cutoffs}\\
 \delta_t&\leq CK^6\log^3(2L)e_0
 \leq\frac Ct g^{13}(\log t)^{30}=o(1).
 \label{eq:lr-marginal-collision-delta}
\end{align}
Here \eqref{eq:lr-marginal-collision} was used.  Thus the same min--max
comparison applies.

It remains to evaluate the free product trace.  By
\eqref{eq:lr-decorated-split}, it has one acoustic band
\(K_{J,L}^N\), one acoustic zero mode, and \(r-1\) optical bands separated
from zero by \(c_J\).  The zero-mode occupation is truncated at \(K\), so
\eqref{eq:uniform-zero-mode-sum} contributes only \(O(\log(K+1))\), also
at \(b=0\). The optical contribution is \(O(L^2e^{-c_Js})\).  The spin
descendants contribute \(O(\log L)\).  Lemma~\ref{lem:lr-bose-traces}
and the exponentially small discarded trace consequently give, uniformly
in \(b\geq0\),
\begin{align}
 \frac1{L^2}\log Z_{L,J,h}^{(S)}(\beta)
 &\leq D_\sigma t^{-\nu}
   \operatorname{Li}_{1+\nu}(e^{-b})+o(t^{-\nu}),
 &&0<\sigma<2,
 \label{eq:lr-stable-box-pressure}\\
 \frac1{L^2}\log Z_{L,J,h}^{(S)}(\beta)
 &\leq\frac{D_2}{t\log t}\operatorname{Li}_2(e^{-b})
   +o((t\log t)^{-1}),
 &&\sigma=2.
 \label{eq:lr-marginal-box-pressure}
\end{align}
Tile a large square by \(L\)-boxes and delete all positive bonds between
them.  To make the comparison explicit for the infinite-range kernel,
first truncate \(J\) at range \(R\), apply
\eqref{eq:duhamel-bond-removal}, and then let \(R\to\infty\). Monotone
convergence of the finite-volume Hamiltonians and partition functions
preserves the inequality.  The box bounds therefore pass to the
thermodynamic pressure.  Since \(f=-\beta^{-1}p\),
\eqref{eq:lr-stable-box-pressure} and
\eqref{eq:lr-marginal-box-pressure} prove
\eqref{eq:lr-stable-pressure-limit} and
\eqref{eq:lr-marginal-pressure-limit}.

title: Proof
body_md:
By \eqref{eq:lr-stable-return}, the constant in both one-sided bounds is
\(D_\sigma\).  Proposition~\ref{prop:lr-pressure} gives
the lower free-energy inequality and Proposition~\ref{prop:lr-variational}
gives the upper one, both uniformly in \(h\geq0\).  Their combination is
\eqref{eq:stable-long-range-limit}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Equations \eqref{eq:lr-marginal-return},
\eqref{eq:lr-marginal-pressure-limit}, and
\eqref{eq:lr-marginal-variational-limit} give the common coefficient
\(D_2=1/(\pi^2a)\), uniformly in \(h\geq0\).  This is exactly
\eqref{eq:marginal-long-range-limit}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Expanding the logarithm in \eqref{eq:spin-wave-free-energy} and using
the return integral \eqref{eq:infinite-heat-return} gives
\[
 -\beta f_J^{\rm sw}(\beta,S)
 =\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\frac{I_J(m\beta S)}m.
\]
The limits and bounds in Lemma~\ref{lem:lr-local-limits} permit dominated
convergence in this series. Its leading coefficient is
\(D_\sigma\zeta(1+2/\sigma)\) for \(0<\sigma<2\), and
\(D_2\zeta(2)\) at \(\sigma=2\), with the respective temperature
scales of Theorem~\ref{thm:long-range-weak-field}. Applying that theorem
at \(h=0\) gives the same leading terms for \(f_J\). Both coefficients
are strictly positive, so the ratio tends to one.
